description:
Side view, left beveled: a long 12 in diameter signal visor drawn as a tube seen from the side, with a diagonal cut across the open (front) end. The top edge is the longer edge and is dimensioned 27"+/-1/16" overall from the back (ear) end. The bottom edge is shorter and is dimensioned 12"+/-1/16" from the back end. A diagonal line joins the end of the bottom edge to the end of the top edge. Dashed lines inside the top and bottom edges show the rolled edge or inner surface, and a dash-dot centerline runs along the axis. Small tabs (ears) are drawn on the back edge near the top and bottom.

Elevation view, left beveled: below the side view, the visor is shown from the front as an elongated oval (the bevel cut opening) with horizontal and vertical centerlines, drawn next to the vertical back edge of the tube with its top and bottom edges dashed. The back edge is tilted from vertical by 3.5 degrees, shown with an angle callout at the bottom left. Caption under it: Left Beveled.

Ear detail: an enlarged profile of one mounting ear, a hook shaped tab on a flat base flange. Overall width is 3/4"+/-1/32". A dimension from the center of the hook radius to the right side is 3/8"+/-1/32". The inner hook radius is 1/8" R+/-1/32" and the outer hook radius is 3/8" R+/-1/32", with the 3/8 in radius shown from a center point on the horizontal centerline.

End (back) view: a circular visor ring with crosshair centerlines and four ears at 45 degree diagonals, labeled See Ear Detail. The ears are spaced 90 degrees apart (90 degree callouts between adjacent ears, with a 45 degree callout from the vertical centerline to the lower ear). The ring is dimensioned 11 3/4"+/-1/16" diameter. The vertical spacing between the upper pair of ears and lower pair of ears is 9"+/-1/16". The diagonal spacing between opposite ears is 12 1/16"+/-1/16".
notes:
1. Left beveled visor shown. See ear detail. Bevel opposite side for right beveled visor.
2. Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.
title: Visor, 12 in Diameter, Beveled (Standard Drawing S-76.6)
summary: Standard drawing S-76.6 shows the 12 in diameter beveled traffic signal visor, drawn in the left beveled version. It gives the side view lengths (27 in top, 12 in bottom), the 3.5 degree back edge angle, the mounting ear detail and the ear layout on the 11 3/4 in ring. A right beveled visor is made by beveling the opposite side. LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 governs all other details.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-76.7, Long Visor, 8 in and 12 in diameter full circle. It shows two long visors, each as a side view paired with an end view. All views are marked Not to Scale.

Long Visor, 8" X 18" full circle, side view: a rectangular tube with overall length 18"+/-1/16". The back edge is tilted 3.5 degrees from vertical, with two small ear tabs on it. Dashed lines near the top and bottom edges, and a dash-dot centerline along the axis.

Long Visor, 8" X 18" full circle, end view: a circular ring dimensioned 8"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals, spaced with 90 degree callouts between adjacent ears. Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Long Visor, 12" X 27" full circle, side view: a tube with overall length 27"+/-1/16" and the same 3.5 degree tilted back edge with two ear tabs. A lens shaped overlap or seam outline is drawn across the lower part of the tube, as it is wrapped from a full circle. Dashed lines at the top and bottom edges and a dash-dot centerline.

Long Visor, 12" X 27" full circle, end view: a circular ring dimensioned 12"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals and four 90 degree callouts. Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Title block: Long Visor, 8" & 12" Diameter Full Circle, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved January 26, 2011 for Amir Sedadi, Interim General Manager, Drawing No. S-76.7, page number 52.
notes:
1. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3 (shown for both the 8 in x 18 in and the 12 in x 27 in long visors).
2. Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.
title: Long Visor, 8 in and 12 in Diameter, Full Circle (Standard Drawing S-76.7)
summary: Standard drawing S-76.7 shows the long full circle signal visors in two sizes, 8 in diameter by 18 in long and 12 in diameter by 27 in long. Each has a side view with a 3.5 degree tilted back edge and an end view with four ears at 90 degree spacing. Ear details are on S-76.3 and all other details are in LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-76.8, Pigeon (Tunnel) Visor, 8 in and 12 in diameter. It shows two tunnel visors, each as a side view paired with an end view. All views are marked Not to Scale.

Visor, 8" X 8" Tunnel, side view: a square looking tube 8"+/-1/16" long. The back edge is tilted 3.5 degrees from vertical, with two ear tabs. Dashed lines near the top and bottom edges and a dash-dot centerline. A dash-dot line below the bottom edge marks the open bottom of the tunnel.

Visor, 8" X 8" Tunnel, end view: a ring dimensioned 8"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals and four 90 degree callouts. The lower part of the ring is open, with a gap between the two lower ears dimensioned 4"+/-1/16". Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Visor, 12" X 12" Tunnel, side view: a tube 12"+/-1/16" long with the same 3.5 degree tilted back edge, two ear tabs, dashed edges, centerline, and open bottom line.

Visor, 12" X 12" Tunnel, end view: a ring dimensioned 12"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals and 90 degree callouts. The open bottom gap between the two lower ears is 5 3/4"+/-1/16". Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Title block: Pigeon (Tunnel) Visor 8" & 12" Diameter, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved January 26, 2011 for Amir Sedadi, Interim General Manager, Drawing No. S-76.8, page number 53.
notes:
1. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3 (shown for both the 8 in x 8 in and the 12 in x 12 in tunnel visors).
2. Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.
title: Pigeon (Tunnel) Visor, 8 in and 12 in Diameter (Standard Drawing S-76.8)
summary: Standard drawing S-76.8 shows the tunnel (pigeon) signal visors for 8 in and 12 in heads, 8 in by 8 in and 12 in by 12 in. Each ring is open at the bottom, with a 4 in gap on the 8 in visor and a 5 3/4 in gap on the 12 in visor. The back edge is tilted 3.5 degrees and four ears sit at 90 degree spacing. Ear details are on S-76.3 and other details are in LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-76.9, Visor 8 in and 12 in diameter full circle (standard short visor). It shows two visors, each as a side view paired with an end view. All views are marked Not to Scale.

Visor, 8" full circle, side view: a short rectangular tube 8"+/-1/16" long. The back edge is tilted 3.5 degrees from vertical with two ear tabs. Dashed lines near top and bottom edges and a dash-dot centerline.

Visor, 8" full circle, end view: a closed circular ring dimensioned 8"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals and 90 degree callouts between ears. Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Visor, 12" full circle, side view: a tube 12"+/-1/16" long with the same 3.5 degree tilted back edge, two ear tabs, dashed edges and centerline.

Visor, 12" full circle, end view: a closed circular ring dimensioned 12"+/-1/16" diameter with four ears at the diagonals and 90 degree callouts. Leader: See Ear Detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3.

Title block: Visor 8" & 12" Diameter Full Circle, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved January 26, 2011 for Amir Sedadi, Interim General Manager, Drawing No. S-76.9, page number 54.
notes:
1. See ear detail on Std. Dwg. No. S-76.3 (shown for both the 8 in and the 12 in full circle visors).
2. Note: Refer to LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06 for all other details.
title: Visor, 8 in and 12 in Diameter, Full Circle (Standard Drawing S-76.9)
summary: Standard drawing S-76.9 shows the standard full circle signal visors, 8 in and 12 in diameter, each 8 in or 12 in long with a 3.5 degree tilted back edge. The end views show closed rings with four ears at 90 degree spacing. Ear details are on S-76.3 and other details are in LADOT Purchase Specification #92-061-06.

description:
Steel Standards drilling detail: a vertical elevation of a round steel pole (shown with a wavy break line at top and bottom) with a vertical centerline and three horizontal reference lines for holes on the centerline. The upper two holes are labeled No. 7 drill, 1/4"-20 N.C. (national coarse) tap, 2 holes. The lowest hole is labeled 1 1/8" drill. The two tapped holes are 6" apart, and the overall distance from the upper tapped hole to the 1 1/8" hole is 9 1/4".

Concrete Standards drilling detail: the same hole pattern on a concrete standard drawn as a fluted or ribbed vertical shaft. The upper two holes are labeled Standard inserts for concrete standards, tapped 1/4"-20 N.C. They are 6" apart. The lowest hole is labeled 5/8" hole. The overall distance from the upper insert to the 5/8" hole is 9 1/4". Long dash-dot lines run from the hole lines to the installation elevation at right.

Typical arrangement (plan): a street corner with a curb return (curved curb) and the crosswalk lines. Two small pushbutton symbols are placed at the corner, one on each crosswalk approach. Leader: Parallel to crosswalk for which intended. A second leader points to the curb (Curb).

Installation elevation: a vertical pole with a rectangular pushbutton unit labeled Pushbutton mounted on it, with the round button at the lower end on the pole centerline. The pushbutton is mounted 3'-6" Typical, marked with an asterisk, measured from the ground line at the pole base up to the button centerline. The pole sits on a stepped base at the ground line.
notes:
* Adjust pushbutton mounting height to 42" above the surface pedestrians are expected to access pushbutton from.
(Callouts on the drawing) Steel standards: No. 7 drill, 1/4"-20 N.C. tap, 2 holes; 1 1/8" drill. Concrete standards: standard inserts for concrete standards, tapped 1/4"-20 N.C.; 5/8" hole. Parallel to crosswalk for which intended. Pushbutton 3'-6" typical*.
title: Pushbutton, Installation (Standard Drawing S-72.0A)
summary: Standard drawing S-72.0A shows how a pedestrian pushbutton is installed on a signal standard. It gives the drilling pattern for steel and concrete standards (two tapped holes 6 in apart and a larger wire hole 9 1/4 in below the upper one), the typical corner arrangement with the button parallel to its crosswalk, and the 3 ft 6 in typical mounting height. The mounting height is to be adjusted to 42 in above the surface pedestrians use to reach the button.

description:
Post-top mounting view: a pedestrian pushbutton station casting seen from the front, with a rectangular sign face above a round button housing. The back of the casting is shaped to fit a 2 1/2" dia. standard (callout at top). The sign face has five panels from top to bottom: (1) walking person symbol with START CROSSING, underlined, and Watch For Vehicles; (2) a flashing hand symbol (labeled FLASHING) with DON'T START, underlined, Finish Crossing, If Started underlined; (3) a timer symbol (labeled TIMER) with TIME REMAINING To Finish Crossing; (4) a steady hand symbol (labeled STEADY) with DON'T CROSS; (5) a long arrow with TO CROSS above and PUSH BUTTON below. Mounting screw holes sit at the corners of the sign. A round pushbutton with four small screw holes around its ring is below the sign. Caption: POST-TOP MOUNTING (See S-51.7 for installation).

Side mounting view (upper right): the same station seen at an angle. The back of the casting is shaped to fit curvature of standard (callout). Caption: SIDE MOUNTING (See S-72.0A for installation).

Side mounting view, lower right: the same station again, captioned SIDE MOUNTING, TYPE 5 AND 6 STANDARDS ONLY (See S-72.0A for installation).

There are no dimensions on the sheet. The text sections at lower left are SIGN, HOUSING and ASSEMBLY. Title block: Pushbutton, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved December 9, 2005 for Frances T. Banerjee, Interim General Manager, Drawing No. S-72.1.1.
notes:
SIGN
1. Pedestrian pushbuttons: see Standard Drawings S-73.0 and S-73.1. Bicycle pushbuttons: see Standard Drawings S-72.2.
2. Mounting hardware consists of four (4) 8-32 x 3/4" long.

HOUSING
Construction, materials and finish painting shall conform to LADOT material specification 92-052-02 or latest version.

ASSEMBLY
Construction, materials and finish painting shall conform to LADOT material specification 92-053-02 or latest version. Pushbuttons shall be 2" in diameter.

View captions: Post-top mounting (see S-51.7 for installation). Side mounting (see S-72.0A for installation). Side mounting, Type 5 and 6 standards only (see S-72.0A for installation). Back of casting shaped to fit 2 1/2" dia. standard (post-top) or to fit curvature of standard (side mounting).
title: Pushbutton (Standard Drawing S-72.1.1)
summary: Standard drawing S-72.1.1 shows the LADOT pedestrian pushbutton station casting, with its sign face and 2 in round button, in post-top and side mounting versions. The back of the casting is shaped to fit a 2 1/2 in diameter standard or the curvature of the standard. Notes cover the sign mounting hardware (four 8-32 x 3/4 in) and the housing and assembly specifications 92-052-02 and 92-053-02.

description:
Sign face, full size elevation: a portrait rectangular sign with rounded corners and a double border (outer edge and a thick inner black border line). Symbol and text are black on white. At the top is a bicycle symbol. Below it in large condensed capital letters: PUSH BUTTON, FOR, GREEN LIGHT, on three lines. Below the text is a black arrow marked with an asterisk (use left, right or double arrow as necessary). A 1/4" inside diameter brass grommet is placed in each of the four corners, 4 places typical.

Dimensions: overall sign width is 5" and the horizontal spacing between grommet centers is 4", with 1/2" from the sign edge to each grommet center. Overall sign height is 7 3/4" and the vertical spacing between grommet centers is 6 3/4", with 1/2" from the sign edge to each grommet center. The outer corner radius is R = 11/32".

Title block: Bicycle Pushbutton Sign, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved July 11, 2008 for Rita L. Robinson, General Manager, Drawing No. S-72.2.
notes:
1. Note: Sign shall be powder coated aluminum with black legend on white background as shown.
2. Material: .063 aluminum.
3. * Use left, right or double arrow as necessary.
(Callout) 1/4" inside diameter brass grommet, 4 places (typ.).
title: Bicycle Pushbutton Sign (Standard Drawing S-72.2)
summary: Standard drawing S-72.2 gives the layout of the LADOT bicycle pushbutton sign, a 5 in by 7 3/4 in aluminum sign reading PUSH BUTTON FOR GREEN LIGHT with a bicycle symbol and a directional arrow. Four 1/4 in brass grommets are set 1/2 in from the edges. The sign is .063 aluminum, powder coated, black legend on white, and the arrow may be left, right or double.

description:
Sign face, full size elevation: a portrait rectangular sign, 5" wide by 7 3/4" tall, with rounded corners and a double border. The legend is black on white with orange hand and timer symbols on black square backgrounds. The face has four panels from top to bottom: (1) a white walking person symbol on black, with START CROSSING underlined and Watch For Vehicles; (2) a flashing orange hand symbol with radiating rays on black (labeled FLASHING) with DON'T START underlined, Finish Crossing, If Started underlined; below it an orange two digit timer symbol 08 on black (labeled TIMER) with TIME REMAINING To Finish Crossing; (3) a steady orange hand symbol on black (labeled STEADY) with DON'T CROSS. There is no TO CROSS PUSH BUTTON panel on this non-actuated version. A 1/4" inside diameter grommet hole is shown in each corner, 4 places (typ.).

Dimensions: overall height 7 3/4" with grommet centers 6 3/4" apart vertically, and 1/2" from the sign edge to each grommet center. Overall width 5" with grommet centers 4" apart horizontally and 1/2" from edge to grommet center. Outer corner radius R = 11/32".

Title block: Pedestrian Pushbutton Sign, Non-Actuated, sheet marker 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 8-9-16 for Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, Drawing No. S-73.0.
notes:
1. Sign shall be .063 aluminum.
2. Powder coated with black legend on white background and orange hand and timer symbols.
(Callout) 1/4" inside diameter [grommet hole], 4 places (typ.).
title: Pedestrian Pushbutton Sign, Non-Actuated (Standard Drawing S-73.0)
summary: Standard drawing S-73.0 gives the layout of the non-actuated pedestrian pushbutton sign, a 5 in by 7 3/4 in .063 aluminum sign. It carries the START CROSSING, DON'T START (flashing hand), TIME REMAINING (timer) and DON'T CROSS (steady hand) messages with orange hand and timer symbols. Four 1/4 in holes are set 1/2 in from the edges and corners have an 11/32 in radius.

description:
Sign face, full size elevation: a portrait rectangular sign, 5" wide by 7 3/4" tall, with rounded corners and a double border. Legend is black on white with orange hand and timer symbols on black square backgrounds. The face has five panels from top to bottom: (1) a white walking person symbol on black, with START CROSSING underlined and Watch For Vehicles; (2) a flashing orange hand symbol with radiating rays (labeled FLASHING) with DON'T START underlined, Finish Crossing, If Started underlined; below it an orange two digit timer symbol 08 (labeled TIMER) with TIME REMAINING To Finish Crossing; (3) a steady orange hand symbol (labeled STEADY) with DON'T CROSS; (4) a bottom panel with PUSH BUTTON above a heavy horizontal arrow and TO CROSS below, with an asterisk at the arrow head (use left, right or double arrow as necessary). A 1/4" inside diameter hole is shown at each corner, 4 places (typ.).

Dimensions: overall height 7 3/4" with hole centers 6 3/4" apart vertically and 1/2" from the sign edge to each hole center. Overall width 5" with hole centers 4" apart horizontally and 1/2" from the edge to each hole center. Outer corner radius R = 11/32".

Title block: Pedestrian Pushbutton Sign, Actuated, sheet marker 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 8-9-16 for Seleta J. Reynolds, General Manager, Drawing No. S-73.1.
notes:
1. Sign shall be .063 aluminum.
2. Powder coated with black legend on white background and orange hand and timer symbols.
* Use left, right or double arrow as necessary.
(Callout) 1/4" inside diameter, 4 places (typ.).
title: Pedestrian Pushbutton Sign, Actuated (Standard Drawing S-73.1)
summary: Standard drawing S-73.1 gives the layout of the actuated pedestrian pushbutton sign, a 5 in by 7 3/4 in .063 aluminum sign. It matches the non-actuated sign (S-73.0) and adds a bottom PUSH BUTTON TO CROSS panel with a left, right or double arrow. Orange hand and timer symbols sit on black squares, with four 1/4 in holes 1/2 in from the edges.

description:
Plan view: two round loops, LOOP-1 and LOOP-2, in a lane. Each loop is 6' in diameter and the clear spacing between the two loops is 8'. Traffic flows left to right, shown by an arrow labeled DIRECTION OF TRAFFIC FLOW. The loop wires leave the loops on the inside edges and join into a single lead-in that runs toward the curb. The lead-in crosses the CURB FACE and ends at a PULLBOX that is 3'-0" MAX. from the curb face. Section cut markers A-A are at each loop, B-B at the diagonal wire runs, C-C at the joined lead-in, and D-D across the curb face at the pullbox (D-D is detailed on sheet 2 of S-70.1A).

Winding details (not to scale): LOOP-1 and LOOP-2 are each drawn as three concentric clockwise turns. The lead-in wires from each loop are twisted clockwise into a pair, at least 2 turns per foot, and run to the pullbox. The four ends are numbered 1, 2, 3 and 4 at the pullbox end.

Section A-A (through the loop slot): a sawcut slot filled with loop sealant to within 1/16" of the top (do not overfill). Slot depth is 3" MIN.* and slot width is 1/2" MAX. Three loop wires are stacked at the bottom of the slot (see note 1).

Section B-B (diagonal run between loops): slot depth 5" MIN.*, slot width 1/2" MAX., two wires at the bottom.

Section C-C (joined lead-in): slot depth 5" MIN.*, slot width 1/2" MAX., four wires shown at the bottom, labeled 8 WIRES MAXIMUM PER SAWCUT SLOT.

Title block: Inductive Loop Installation, sheet 1 of 2, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved July 9, 2008 for Rita L. Robinson, General Manager, Drawing No. S-70.1A.
notes:
* Depth of slot not to exceed depth of pavement. For P.C.C. (concrete) surfaces, the minimum cover above loop wire shall be 2.5" minimum.

Notes:
1. Install 3 clockwise turns of loop wire for each detector, unless otherwise shown on signal plan.
2. See LADOT material specification No. 92-081-05 or latest revision.
3. Any non-round shaped loops must conform to all other specifications shown on this standard drawing.

Callouts: Fill slot with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill). Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair. To pullbox. Direction of traffic flow. Curb face. Pullbox 3'-0" max. from curb face.
title: Inductive Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1A, Sheet 1 of 2)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.1A, sheet 1, shows the layout of a pair of 6 ft round inductive loops spaced 8 ft apart with a twisted lead-in running to a pullbox within 3 ft of the curb face. It gives the winding order (3 clockwise turns per detector) and sawcut slot sections with 3 in or 5 in minimum depth, 1/2 in maximum width, and a limit of 8 wires per slot. Slots are filled with loop sealant to within 1/16 in of the top.

description:
Section D-D (not to scale): a cut through the curb, gutter and roadway at the pullbox. At left, the pullbox pit with its lid and the curb and gutter, with sidewalk paving, sits on rock base. A 2" PVC or 2" PVC FLEX conduit leaves the bottom of the pullbox, curves under the curb and gutter and runs to the stub-out in the street. The pavement opening is at least 42" MIN. from the curb face and at least 18" MIN. from the edge of the gutter. A hot patch asphalt concrete patch is placed in the opening, which is 16" MAX. wide. Existing pavement lies on both sides.

Conduit detail (not to scale): a longitudinal section at the stub-out. Existing pavement is at left and right, with HOT PATCH ASPHALT CONCRETE 4" thick over 1" of SAND in the opening. A 2" PVC or 2" PVC FLEX conduit rises at 45 degrees from a minimum 18" below the street surface through sub base and exits at the surface, where the loop wires (marked *) continue horizontally into the sawcut slot filled with LOOP SEALANT. Labels: existing pavement, sub base, sand, loop sealant, loop wires, hot patch asphalt concrete.

Stub-out detail, top view (not to scale): a rectangular hot patch asphalt concrete patch within existing pavement, 16" MAX. long and 12" MAX. wide. A PVC conduit enters from the left as dashed lines and ends in the patch.

Title block: Inductive Loop Installation, sheet 2 of 2, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.1A.
notes:
Notes: Perform loop installation in the following order:
1. Open the pavement at least 42" from curb face and at least 18" from edge of gutter using a star drill or a jack hammer (asphalt concrete only). Open no more than a 12" x 16" area. In cases where there is a concrete bus pad adjacent to the gutter, install the stubout beyond the edge of the bus pad.
2. Install 2" PVC (SC80) or PVC flex (SC40) from the pullbox pit with a 45 degree elbow at the stub-out as shown. Depth of the conduit shall be at least 18" below the street grade.
3. Patch street using hot patch asphalt concrete and sand as shown.
4. Install duct seal where wires enter 2" PVC or 2" PVC flex.
5. Fill sawcut slot with Caltrans approved hot-melt rubberized asphalt sealant.
* No more than 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out.
title: Inductive Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1A, Sheet 2 of 2)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.1A, sheet 2, shows how to connect inductive loop wires to a pullbox with a conduit and stub-out in the street. It gives the pavement opening limits (at least 42 in from the curb face, 18 in from the gutter, no more than 12 in by 16 in), conduit type and depth (2 in PVC at least 18 in deep) and the patch and sealant materials. A five step installation order and a limit of 8 loops or 16 wires per stub-out are also given.

description:
Plan view: a 6' diameter preformed loop, drawn as a dashed circle with a dashed diagonal bar, connected by a dashed lead-in to a PULLBOX that is 3'-0" MAX. from the CURB FACE. Section A-A is cut along the lead-in path.

Preformed loop detail: the loop is a circular ring built from 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose, with four expansion joints and CPVC (chlorinated PVC) tees and a CPVC cross on the ring, a diagonal 3/4" O.D. hose across the ring, and a 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose lead-in leaving at the CPVC cross, ending in a twisted tail.

Winding details (not to scale): the wire is wound in several clockwise turns inside the loop, with the ends twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair and run TO PULLBOX. The two ends are marked 1 and 2.

Section A-A (typical, not to scale): from the pullbox at left, DETECTOR LOOP CONDUCTORS pass from the pullbox through a Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see note 7), under the curb and gutter, then in a 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose to the detector, within the pavement, running PER PLAN to the loop. The loop sits in the pavement with 4" MIN. between the pavement surface and the loop.

Title block: Preformed Loop Installation, sheet 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 2-16-99, signed Frances T. Banerjee, General Manager, Drawing No. S-70.1E. Revision 1: Rev. distance, JV, 5-6-08.
notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropylene, with an O.D. of 3/4" inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" Schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wires in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose seamless fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a Schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.
7. The 3/8" O.D. lead-in hose shall be installed in 2" PVC conduit between pullbox and entry to pavement slab. Loop shall be attached to top of reinforcing bars when used in the pavement slab.

Callouts: Expansion joint. CPVC tee. CPVC cross. 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. Twisted tail. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turn per ft.) into a pair. To pullbox. Detector loop conductors. Schedule 80 PVC 2" conduit (see note 7). Pavement. 4" min.
title: Preformed Loop Installation (Standard Drawing S-70.1E)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.1E shows a preformed 6 ft inductive loop built from 3/4 in O.D. hose with expansion joints, CPVC tees and cross, and a 3/8 in O.D. asphalt filled lead-in hose. It gives the winding details, a section from the pullbox through a 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit to the loop, and seven notes covering materials, #16 TFFN wire with four turns, sealing with rubberized asphalt, and expansion joints. The pullbox is within 3 ft of the curb face.

description:
Table 1, loop turns: two columns, LENGTH OF LOOP and NUMBER OF TURNS. Row 1: less than 40' = 2 turns. Row 2: 40' or more (greater than or equal to 40') = 1 turn.

Winding detail, 2 turns: an elongated slot shaped loop drawn as two nested long U shaped runs with direction arrows. The wire goes up one side, around the rounded end, and back down, twice, then leaves as a twisted pair (shown as twisted tail at lower left). Caption 2 TURNS.

Winding detail, 1 turn: a single elongated U shaped run with direction arrows, leaving as a twisted pair at lower left. Caption 1 TURN.

Saw slot detail: a long narrow slot, plan view, with semicircular ends. Width is 6' and the end radius is R=3'. Length is AS SPECIFIED ON PLAN, shown with a vertical dimension line. Depth callouts: Depth=3" Min. for the slot along the loop sides, and Depth=5" Min. for the diagonal saw cut that leaves the slot at the lower left toward the lead-in.

Symbol: the plan symbol for this loop, a tall narrow rounded rectangle (slot shape) with a leader.

notes:

title: Transit Priority Loop (Standard Drawing S-70.1F)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.1F shows the elongated transit priority loop, a slot shaped saw cut 6 ft wide with 3 ft end radius and a length set on the plan. Loops shorter than 40 ft get 2 turns of wire and loops of 40 ft or longer get 1 turn. Slot depth is 3 in minimum along the loop and 5 in minimum for the diagonal lead-in cut.

description:
Four wiring hookup diagrams for loop detector lead-in cable, each showing loops (numbered circles with three turns) at left, twisted lead-in pairs, a cable jacket and the color coded pairs at right. In every diagram a drain wire leaves the cable and is connected to earth ground at the controller cabinet.

One-loop hookup, 2 pair cable: loop 1 is connected by its twisted pair to the cable. At the far end the pairs are BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1) and ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2). The loop uses one pair. Label: DO NOT CONNECT UNUSED PAIR. Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Two-loop hookup, 2 pair cable: loops 1 and 2 each connect by a twisted pair to the cable. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1) and ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Three-loop hookup, 3 pair cable: loops 1, 2 and 3 each connect by a twisted pair. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1), ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2), GREEN/WHITE (PAIR 3). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Four-loop hookup, 4 pair cable: loops 1 to 4 each connect by a twisted pair. Pairs: BLUE/WHITE (PAIR 1), ORANGE/WHITE (PAIR 2), GREEN/WHITE (PAIR 3), BROWN/WHITE (PAIR 4). Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.

Title block: System Detector Loop Lead-In Cable (2,3,4 Pair), sheet 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved February 25, 2005, Wayne K. Tanda, General Manager, Drawing No. S-70.2.
notes:
1. This standard drawing describes a two, three or four pair loop detector lead-in cable, individually shielded and jacketed and suitable for installation in a pavement sawcut, conduit, or direct burial.
2. The detector lead-in cable can be wired in either a single, double, triple or quadruple channel configuration.
3. Electrical connections shall be carefully soldered and waterproofed.
4. See LADOT material specification No. 92-082-03 or latest revision.
5. Loop numbers shown are typical.
6. System loops use a single pair for each loop.
Callouts: Do not connect unused pair. Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.
title: System Detector Loop Lead-In Cable, 2, 3 and 4 Pair (Standard Drawing S-70.2)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.2 shows how to hook up one to four detector loops to a 2, 3 or 4 pair lead-in cable. Pairs are color coded blue/white, orange/white, green/white and brown/white, each loop uses one pair, and the drain wire is grounded at the controller cabinet. Notes cover cable construction, soldering and waterproofing, and LADOT specification 92-082-03.

description:
Schematic wiring diagram titled Actuation / Phase Loops, with a dashed CURB LINE across the lower part and four arrows labeled DIRECTION OF TRAVEL (pointing right) at upper right.

Loops: eight loops are drawn as coil symbols in two columns. Left column: LOOP 1 (terminals 1 and 2), LOOP 3 (terminals 5 and 6), LOOP 5 (terminals 9 and 10), LOOP 7 (terminals 13 and 14). Right column: LOOP 2 (terminals 3 and 4), LOOP 4 (terminals 7 and 8), LOOP 6 (terminals 11 and 12), LOOP 8 (terminals 15 and 16). Nested lead wires run down from each loop terminal past the curb line. Below the curb line, solid dots mark splices where leads of adjacent loops are joined in series, and four more pairs of dots mark the connections to four twisted pairs.

Cable: the four twisted pairs enter a 4 PAIR CABLE with pairs labeled BLUE/WHITE, ORANGE/WHITE, GREEN/WHITE and BROWN/WHITE at the right. A drain wire is connected to earth ground at the controller cabinet.

Title block: Multi-Pair Loop Lead-In Cable, sheet 1/1, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved June 26, 2008, Rita L. Robinson, General Manager, Drawing No. S-70.3. Drawn MT 05-07-08.
notes:
1. Connect two to four loops in series to each pair, do not use parallel connections.
2. Do not connect any unused cable pairs.
3. Typical installation shown. Two or three pair cable may be used when shown on signal plan.
Callouts: Actuation / phase loops. Direction of travel. Curb line. 4 pair cable. Blue/white, orange/white, green/white, brown/white. Drain wire connected to earth ground at controller cabinet.
title: Multi-Pair Loop Lead-In Cable (Standard Drawing S-70.3)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.3 is a wiring schematic that connects up to eight actuation or phase loops in series pairs to a 4 pair lead-in cable (blue/white, orange/white, green/white, brown/white). Loops are connected in series, never in parallel, and unused pairs are not connected. Two or three pair cable may be used when shown on the signal plan.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 1 of 3. It has two installations, with sections.

LRT detector for existing track (embedded), plan: two parallel embedded tracks run vertically. Between them is an octagonal saw cut loop 30" across, marked 4-turns of wire, with detector wires installed in saw cut (5" deep). A lead-in runs 36" from the loop down to a detector handhole type 'A', then horizontally to a termination pullbox with two conduits leaving it. Section C-C is cut through the loop, and section D-D is looked at from the handhole.

Section C-C: a saw cut slot filled with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill). The slot is 5" max. deep with the wires in the lower part at least 3" min. below the surface, and 1/2" max. wide. Four wires are shown stacked at the bottom.

Section D-D, embedded track: layers P.C.C. (concrete), A.B. (aggregate base) and subbase, with subballast bed, P.C.C. or asphalt concrete surface, embedded track rails, the saw cut loop (5" max. below surface) and the detector handhole type 'A'. A 2" PVC Sched. 80 conduit, 30" deep, runs from the handhole to the termination pull box, with 30" min. cover.

LRT detector for new track (ballasted), plan: a rectangular concrete slab 40" wide by 80" long between two train tracks, crossing concrete track ties. A circular preformed loop 30" in diameter (4-turns of wire, pre-formed loop) sits in the slab, with a lead 36" long to the detector handhole type 'A' at the slab edge. Another run goes to a termination pullbox with two conduits. Reference: See Detail 'A'. Section B-B cut.

Section B-B, ballasted track: preformed loop in a slab at the rail, over concrete track tie and ballasted or concrete track bed. 2" PVC Sched. 80 conduit, 30" deep, from the detector handhole type 'A' to the termination pull box (30" min.).

Detail 'A', ballasted track: the slab with the loop inside, top of slab even with rail, 2" from the top of slab to the loop, and slab depth varies.

Title block: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 1/3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, approved 8-8-2014, Jon Kirk Mukri, General Manager, Drawing No. S-70.4A. Drawn MT 8-7-14, T.E. BC 8-7-14, Pr. T.E. SS 8-7-14.
notes:
1. Saw cut loops (octagonal or circular) to be used for existing installations only.
2. See LADOT Std. Dwg. S-70.1.A for inductive loop installation details not shown hereon.
(Notes for the new track (ballasted) installation)
1. Preformed loop to be used for all new construction.
2. See current LADOT material specification for traffic loop.
3. See page 2 and 3 for preformed LRT loop details.
Callouts: 4-turns of wire. Embedded track. Install detector wires in saw cut (5" deep). Fill slot with loop sealant to within 1/16" of top (do not overfill). Termination pullbox. Conduit. Detector handhole type 'A'.
title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop (Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Sheet 1 of 3)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.4A, sheet 1, shows detector loops for light rail trains. For existing embedded track a 30 in octagonal saw cut loop with 4 turns is used. For new ballasted track a preformed 30 in circular loop in a 40 in by 80 in concrete slab is used. Both connect through a type A detector handhole and 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit 30 in deep to a termination pullbox. Saw cut loops are for existing installations only.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 2 of 3.

LRT detector for new track (embedded), plan: two parallel embedded tracks run vertically. Between them is a circular preformed loop 30" in diameter with 4-turns of wire, marked section C-C. A lead 36" long runs from the loop down to a detector handhole type 'A', then horizontally to a termination pullbox with two conduits leaving it. Section A-A is cut at the handhole.

Section A-A, embedded track: layers of P.C.C., A.B. (aggregate base) and subbase over a subballast bed, with a P.C.C. or asphalt concrete surface and embedded track rails. The preformed loop is set in the surface between the rails, with 2" dimensioned at the top. The detector handhole type 'A' connects by 2" PVC Sched. 80 conduit, 30" deep, to the termination pull box, with 30" min. cover at the pull box.

LRT preformed loop details: a block of text notes (notes 1 to 6) on materials and installation of the preformed loop. Continues on sheet 3 of 3.

Title block: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 2/3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.4A.
notes:
Notes (new track, embedded):
1. Preformed loop to be used for new installations in embedded track.
2. No rebar or metal of any kind other than the track rails shall be placed within three feet (3') horizontally or vertically from LRT loop.
3. See page 2 and 3 for preformed LRT loop details.

LRT preformed loop details, notes:
1. Pre-formed loop shall be constructed from 1/2" I.D. polypropolene, with an O.D. of 3/4 inch.
2. Loop is to have one continuous #16 TFFN wire through the loop head and lead-in to prevent loop malfunction due to splicing. Loop shall have four (4) turns of wire.
3. The conduit shall be completely filled with hot, rubberized asphalt which will allow the loop to retain flexibility once cooled, prevent incursion of moisture and set the wire turns firmly in place.
4. Each loop head shall be provided with a 5" contraction/expansion joint to allow for movement of pavement and to prevent breakage of the wire and/or conduit. The joint is to have a 9" long by 3/4" schedule 80 PVC cover slide to be placed over the joint for protection from the elements.
5. Encase lead-in wire in a non-conductive 250 psi flex hose, seamless, with fiber braid reinforcement and a non-conductive seamless extruded urethane non-perforated jacket. Fill lead-in hose completely with hot rubberized asphalt. Twist wires at least two times per foot for entire run. Attach lead-in to loop head with a schedule 80 CVPC tee and a CVPC adapter bushing.
6. Any variation to the installation as described above shall be approved by the design engineer prior to installation.
title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop (Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Sheet 2 of 3)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.4A, sheet 2, shows the detector loop for new embedded light rail track, a 30 in circular preformed loop with 4 turns of wire between the rails and a 36 in lead to a type A handhole. A 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit 30 in deep runs to the termination pullbox. No rebar or other metal except the rails may be within 3 ft of the loop. Six notes cover the preformed loop materials.

description:
This sheet is Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 3 of 3.

LRT preformed loop details (cont'd), loop: a circular loop 30" in diameter made of 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose, with an expansion joint and a CVCC tee on the ring. A 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose runs from the tee to the Type A Handhole and ends in a twisted tail.

Winding details (not to scale): the wire is wound in four clockwise turns around the loop. The ends are twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair and run to the Type A Handhole, ends labeled 1 and 2.

Type 'A' LRT detector handhole, section: a precast reinforced concrete box with a 9" throat diameter, set under a cast iron frame and cover at the surface. Overall height is 12" from the surface to the bottom of the box, with a box internal depth of 11-3/8", 8" min. clear depth below the cover and a 6" min. clean, crushed rock sump below the box. The backfill at the surface is ballast, PCC or hot AC to match adjacent roadbed material, with a loop sealant layer 4" min. at the top. The box sits in Portland cement concrete, 3" min. around the handhole. Box width is 10-3/8" with 1" walls. Cables of shielded loop conductor pairs enter at the side and splices are made inside the handhole. Conduit to termination pullbox is 2" Schedule 80 PVC, 30" deep, entering through the bottom.

Handhole cover, plan: a cast iron frame and cover with a cross hatched top and a rectangular label reading LADOT. Cover diameter is 11-1/8" and the overall frame diameter is 14-1/4".

Title block: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop, sheet 3/3, City of Los Angeles Department of Transportation, Drawing No. S-70.4A.
notes:
1. Splices shall only be made in the handhole.
2. Splices shall be soldered and water proofed.
Callouts: 3/4" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose. 3/8" O.D. asphalt rubber filled hydraulic hose to Type A Handhole. CVCC tee. Expansion joint. Twisted tail. Twisted clockwise (at least 2 turns per ft.) into a pair. Ballast, PCC or hot AC to match adjacent roadbed material. Precast reinforced concrete box. Conduit to termination pullbox. 2" Schedule 80 PVC (30" deep). Clean, crushed rock sump. Loop sealant. Cables of shielded loop conductor pairs. Portland cement concrete. 3" min. around the handhole. Cast iron frame and cover.
title: Light Rail Train (LRT) Track Detector Loop (Standard Drawing S-70.4A, Sheet 3 of 3)
summary: Standard drawing S-70.4A, sheet 3, gives the preformed LRT loop details (30 in loop of 3/4 in hose with a 3/8 in lead-in and 4 clockwise turns) and the Type A detector handhole. The handhole is a precast concrete box with a 9 in throat, cast iron LADOT cover, 6 in minimum crushed rock sump and 2 in Schedule 80 PVC conduit 30 in deep. Splices are made only in the handhole, soldered and waterproofed.

description:
Isometric view of the cabinet: a tall rectangular outdoor cabinet shown with its front door and rear door open slightly. Overall dimensions are 20" wide on the front face, 17" deep and 35" high. Features called out: Removable lifting plates per S-68.1 on top; Identification (required on front door), a CITY OF LOS ANGELES plate on the front door; Police door with shroud to provide access to switches and indicators only (required on front door); Front door; Rear door; Fan Vent on the side; Louvered vents with 20 in2 min. flow area (required in front door) near the bottom of the front door; and a door handle with the note: Cabinet doors shall be secured by a 3-point latch mechanism. Latch handle shall be equipped with hasp for addition of pad lock (required on front and rear doors).

Bottom view (post-top mount): a square plan of the cabinet base, 10" from center to edge each way as shown (10" and 6 1/2" each side of center line). It has a central 3 1/2" dia. opening, a 5 1/4" dia. bolt circle, four 9/16" dia. holes equally spaced at 45 degrees on the bolt circle, and four 1/8" dia. drainage holes for the mounting adapter. Hole positions are dimensioned 6 1/2" and 6 1/2" horizontally from the centerline, 1 3/4" and 8 1/2" vertically, and 3 1/2" between the two upper and lower drainage holes.

Cabinet details: dimension tolerance +/-0.125 inch.

title: 337 Cabinet, Post-Top Mounted (Standard Drawing S-75.9A)
summary: Standard drawing S-75.9A shows the Type 337 post-top mounted traffic signal controller cabinet, 20 in wide, 17 in deep and 35 in high. It calls out lifting plates, doors, police door, vents, 3-point latch with padlock hasp, and gives the bottom bolt pattern for post-top mounting.
